name: Peach Hour
tagline: A small sunlit village you can turn, and a sun you can move.
summary: The company is shown as a miniature hill village on a stone turntable, built from three.js primitives and graded like false-colour infrared film. Each product is one house, carrying its real logo. Precision and patience are shown, not claimed: the visitor turns the model, drags the sun from sunrise to dusk, and the name in the sky is lit from wherever the sun stands.
voice: Warm, short, sure of itself, and it never sells. Example: "Small, exact software that pays for itself."
motion: Slow and sunlit: letters warm from weight 300 to 820, layers drift at different depths, and shutters swing open on each product, all settling on long expo-out curves.
sound: Silent. Nothing plays unless a visitor turns it on, and the homepage offers nothing to turn on.
mark: A round-arched window with the sun rising on its sill, beside a lowercase "albretsen" and a terracotta "AS" outlined from Nunito 820.
